This is a synchronous trusted owner contribution, with no REST endpoint or replacement of the standalone scoped-access query. Contract methods are `Prepared prepare()` and `Contribution contribute(Prepared prepared, TopologyScopedAccessContract.Request request)`. A caller-supplied marker, record, principal, user id or prior PERMIT cannot establish origin. Expensive native verification remains before admission through F.prepare; contribution requires the existing writable physical READ COMMITTED transaction and all existing fences. No REQUIRES_NEW, nested transaction or caller-controlled s/u is admitted.

Extend the existing F participant with an opaque `QualifiedClaimPair` prepared from one genuine Prepared and the exact Request. Resolve user identity only from the actual F contribution. Derive both AuthorizationEvaluationRequests internally, with the same actor, permission, `STATION_GRAPH_REVISION` resource type and facility resource reference; company scope is CUSTOM `topology-company:<companyPartyId>`, facility scope is FACILITY `<facilityId>`. Map AUTHOR, PUBLISH, READ_CURRENT, READ_HISTORY, LIST_HISTORY, WITHDRAW, REACTIVATE and TRANSFER to the existing suffixes author, publish, read-current, read-history, list-history, withdraw, reactivate and transfer. No arbitrary code, wildcard, scope, resource type, context attributes or actor override is accepted.

Pair creation calls F.contribute exactly once, preserving one database s, finite conservative u, backend PID and XID. The pair owns both exact requests and the same genuine binding/context/transaction resource. Add `loadQualifiedPair(pair, request)` to the existing reader; consume the pair once, validate both canonical requests and all existing origin/catalog/fence rules, load two fresh bounded graphs in this same transaction, then recheck actual context, catalog and transaction before returning to the trusted adapter. Factor existing private qualified-loading checks where necessary; retain the original one-request entry and its one-shot semantics. Do not manufacture two public Contributions or call qualifyClaims twice. SQL/storage/catalog/coverage failures abort the pair and never expose a partial successful result. Evaluate both graphs synchronously at the captured s using the existing pure evaluator. Both must be PERMIT: an explicit DENY in either result wins over the other result; otherwise any INDETERMINATE is non-permitting; otherwise a missing grant/other DENY remains DENY. No successful Boolean is returned from a partially evaluated pair. Hold all locks to physical commit; this internal contribution itself does not commit or publish a client result.

The exported immutable scalar Contribution contains only bindingId, sessionId, userId, operation, derived permissionCode, companyPartyId, facilityId, companyDecision, facilityDecision, combinedDecision, sampledAt, validUntil, backendPid and transactionId. Use contract-local decision enums PERMIT/DENY/INDETERMINATE and the existing Operation; no domain aggregate, JPA entity, AuthorizationEvidence, grants/rules/attribute maps, raw claims, token, issuer/JTI, credential/link details or free-text diagnostic crosses the module boundary. Validate non-null identity/references and s<u on construction; no mutable collections. A constructible scalar export is data, not a transferable attestation. Future K must call the actual configured trusted contributor and revalidate its own coordinator context; never accept caller-constructed Contribution as authority. I exports Identity's bound only, not a complete multi-owner u or final publication permit.

**1. Source-backed semantic separation.** `StationInternalGraphRevision` and `StationInternalGraph` are pure-Java immutable declarations (DRAFT/COMPLETE, supplied source classification, evidence and predecessor intent); `StationInternalGraphRevisionRepositoryPort` and `JdbcStationInternalGraphRevisionRepositoryAdapter` store exact canonical V1 bytes/digest and intentionally do NOT publish, enforce a head, authenticate a source or resolve an expected predecessor. `V20261011_002__p25_topology_station_graph_revisions.sql` is append-only (PK facility_id/revision_id, digest check, update/delete/truncate rejection). `V20261018_002__p25_topology_facility_owner_generations.sql` records live owner generations, **not** publication epochs. `ProtectedStationAdmissionCoordinator` already provides I→Party→Facility opaque admission and one physical common sample; its public `Contribution` is only scalars, not transferable authority. `ProtectedOperationDataSource` currently rejects all DML during admitted execution; `ProtectedTransactionExecutor` requires a flush, one closed final scalar guard, observed physical COMMIT and a 500ms aggregate deadline. None of these pieces proves publication or protected current/history exposure. Do not alter the meaning of K or the old revision adapter/codec.

**2. Owner and aggregate design.** Topology is the sole owner of station-graph publication state, head/epoch, predecessor-CAS, immutable publication events and exact current/history resolution. Identity owns permission and source-authentication evidence; Party owns company eligibility; Topology Facility owns authoritative facility-to-owner assignment and generation; Platform owns JDBC/transaction mechanics **without** business rules. Domain additions are immutable `StationGraphPublicationHead` and `StationGraphPublicationEvent` with explicit facility/revision, monotonic epoch, ACTIVE/WITHDRAWN status, optional preceding revision, supported action and validated provenance. A private Topology outbound port `StationGraphProtectedPublicationPort` acquires a non-forgeable, same-thread/physical-tx owner ticket before the common K sample, reads exact head/predecessor and performs only compiled, typed provisional operations. The inbound `ProtectedStationGraphOperationUseCase` accepts typed, bounded commands and never grants from caller-created identity/party/owner scalars. `ProtectedStationGraphOperationService` composes K `prepare→acquire`, then Topology head/revision/event relation acquisition **before** K `collect`, performs legitimate work in the one protected executor transaction, and returns fully materialized immutable data **only after physical commit**. No REST endpoint is invented in L; consumer API/OpenAPI work belongs to its registered later owner stage.

**3. Exact new PostgreSQL schema (fresh-schema proposal, NOT present).** Reserve only `V20261018_003__p25_topology_protected_station_graph_operations.sql` after verifying the live chain remains at `V20261018_002` before implementation; never edit earlier migrations or require synthetic production backfill. Create `public.hidra_topology_station_graph_head`: `facility_id varchar(80) PRIMARY KEY`, `revision_id text NOT NULL`, `head_epoch bigint NOT NULL CHECK (head_epoch>0)`, `state varchar(16) NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('ACTIVE','WITHDRAWN'))`, `last_event_id uuid NOT NULL`; composite FK `(facility_id,revision_id)` to immutable `hidra_topology_station_graph_revision(facility_id,revision_id)`. No FK to mutable facility master: permanent publication history and ABA tombstones must survive owner lifecycle; K still proves currently live facility on every protected action. Create `public.hidra_topology_station_graph_operation_event`: `event_id uuid PRIMARY KEY`, `facility_id varchar(80) NOT NULL`, `event_kind varchar(16) NOT NULL`, `resulting_epoch bigint`, `prior_revision_id text`, `resulting_revision_id text`, `actor_binding_id varchar(80) NOT NULL`, `actor_session_id varchar(80) NOT NULL`, `actor_user_id varchar(80) NOT NULL`, `company_party_id varchar(80) NOT NULL`, `party_generation bigint NOT NULL`, `facility_generation bigint NOT NULL`, `sampled_at timestamptz NOT NULL`, `valid_until timestamptz NOT NULL`, `backend_pid integer NOT NULL`, `transaction_id bigint NOT NULL`; DB positive/range/action constraints, unique `(facility_id,resulting_epoch)` for nonnull epochs, composite FK of every nonnull resulting revision to immutable revision PK, and an immutable FK `head.last_event_id→event.event_id` (non-deferrable). For a first published head, guarded same-transaction insertion orders the event before the head; later events and CAS update the head. Add appropriate facility/epoch ordered-history indexes; event rows immutable by database UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE rejection, head deletion/TRUNCATE prohibited and epoch strictly monotonic by both CAS and a database row-transition guard. Explicitly bind head to ledger's same facility/epoch/revision with relational constraints or a reviewed in-transaction validation trigger; a mere event-ID FK is insufficient. Reject unauthorized direct DML/DDL via role grants, trigger/function owner separation, and metadata/role/trigger integrity validation in the actual nonowner runtime test. Avoid fabricated permissions or data-dictionary output. Existing revision table is untouched.

**4. Protected operation/epoch semantics.** Supported private commands are `AUTHOR` (authenticated append of immutable draft/source-declared revision only; no implicit publication/head), `PUBLISH` (COMPLETE + STRUCTURALLY_QUALIFIED revision and valid evidence; exact predecessor from the immutable revision payload; first head expected epoch 0/null predecessor or existing ACTIVE head expected epoch/current revision; validated event + CAS), `WITHDRAW` (retain revision/history, switch ACTIVE→WITHDRAWN at expected epoch), `REACTIVATE` (WITHDRAWN→ACTIVE for that same integrity-checked current revision at expected epoch), `READ_CURRENT` (return only ACTIVE exact head revision), `READ_HISTORY` and `LIST_HISTORY` (authorized exact revision and deterministic bounded event/revision history). All use the existing operation-specific Identity permission, exact facility and authoritative matching company owner from K; unauthorized existence/counts/list cursors are never disclosed. `TRANSFER` is a configured Identity permission **only**, not an evidenced Topology station-owner transfer mutation; L must reject its runtime command as explicitly unsupported, not manufacture Party/Facility ownership changes or call it successful transfer. Historical exact revision storage remains available to existing internal owners without being reinterpreted as published history. No automatic retry or idempotent success claim after an indeterminate COMMIT.

**5. Physical sequence and concurrency.** The only accepted order is: outside transaction verify genuine authentication and prepare K; start `ProtectedTransactionExecutor.execute` in one writable READ COMMITTED physical tx; K `acquire` obtains all Identity→Party→Facility NOWAIT fences; still in ADMITTING, acquire `hidra_topology_station_graph_revision`, `..._head` and `..._operation_event` table fences in a fixed order with NOWAIT, and validate no pre-admission user statement/dirty JPA state; only then K `collect` establishes common actual PostgreSQL `s` and conservative `u`, both owner generations and both Identity permit results. Topology reads head/revision through its retained real ticket (no new clock or transaction) and checks exact expected `epoch` + predecessor + state. If a mutating command, transition through **one bounded, explicitly scoped PROVISIONAL phase** to perform only the operation's reviewed parameterized revision/head/event statements, guarded by the actual unforgeable admission and fenced head; require exactly the expected affected rows and epoch increment without wraparound. Platform must recognize only those reviewed owner call sites/statements and disallow arbitrary SQL, batch, writable CTE, dynamic callbacks, DDL, hidden JPA flush, additional connection, late locks, savepoints or role changes. All denied/caught errors poison and roll back. Admission remains strictly read-only outside the finite provisional phase; K tests and unchanged diagnostic `execute` paths must remain green. Fail conflicting writer-first NOWAIT safely; reader-first holds fences through commit and blocks competing revocation/owner/epoch writers. No speculative timestamp/decision from caller.

**6. Exactly one final physical guard.** Before final GUARD: validate the original opaque K ticket remains current, physical connection/PID/XID unchanged, relation-fence census complete, current Party and Facility generations/owner unchanged, intended head+event+predecessor/epoch and revision digest coherent, no unexplained JPA dirty changes, no previous SQL/role/transaction escape; flush in the existing executor's order. The *last application SQL* is one closed, scalar, parameterized PostgreSQL statement, using MATERIALIZED `clock_timestamp()` `t` and asserting `s <= t AND t < u` together with matching fresh head epoch/state/event, immutable revision identity, actual owner/permission-relevant fence predicates and physical PID/XID. No SQL, lazy load, owner lookup, recheck, result-set leak or arbitrary callback after that guard, except provider physical COMMIT/cleanup. One integer/bool closed scalar is required, and a false/missing/ambiguous guard poisons the whole tx. The K 500ms aggregate budget, 250ms lock, 750ms statement and 1000ms idle timeouts and final-guard/commit uncertainty classification are retained, not stretched to make fixtures pass. Record microsecond PostgreSQL timestamp precision and equality at s explicitly. A successful return is evidence only of observed physical commit, not SITE/industrial qualification.
